mission: Build the fractal Google Maps of law: a zoomable, multi-level, multi-view map of Swiss Federal Supreme Court case law (2000-present) plus user-imported corpora, whose navigation/ordering is demonstrably more useful to jurists than a simple whole-document semantic map, with all claims anchored to structures actually present in the corpus.

corpus.question: RESUME (RUN_38046875969, direction v36) scoped to PRODUCING AND DURABLY PUBLISHING the full-corpus artifacts the factory actually consumes, whose accepted-mount presence is currently unverifiable: (1) bge<->bger canonical ID mapping (canonical corpus uses bge_ IDs, downstream/evaluation uses bger_ IDs; no mapping exists); (2) durable full-corpus normalized artifacts for ALL years 2000-2026 (accepted mount contains only test/sample slices plus raw/yearly/bger_2020..2024.jsonl; 2022-2026 parquet and pre-2020 yearly files are absent); (3) section extraction at full scale (Sachverhalt/Erwaegungen/Dispositiv). Do NOT spend cycles on generic re-verification of already-claimed normalization, and do NOT own citation-graph reconstruction (assigned to frontier team citation-graph-reconstruction). Deliverable must be a published, checksummed artifact set with per-year coverage accounting, not a regenerated ephemeral workspace.
corpus.priority_rationale: Every downstream lane and both frontier charters are blocked on these three concrete artifacts. Corpus is the critical path.

legal-distance.question: EXHAUSTED for the current direction (former RUN demoted per RUN_38046875969). ACCEPTED and CORRECTED evidence: dense center_projected FAILS the jurist gate at all scales (JP 0.05-0.43); TF-IDF citation hybrids PASS and BEAT the simple semantic-map baseline (primary mode cited_decisions_tfidf_outcome_hybrid_0.5); true OOS jurist-preference ceiling ~0.53 < 0.7 factory target (accepted negative, closes dense-as-primary). Dense citation-heritage superiority is RETRACTED at scale: full-174k AUC 0.482 FAIL (vs threshold 0.75); the earlier 0.79-0.85 PASS was partial-cohort (2000-2021, 36-54% coverage) and does not generalize. Re-activation trigger ONLY: durable corpus deliveries (sections + bge/bger mapping + full years) OR accepted results from frontier teams (citation-graph-reconstruction, norms-at-issue-coarse). No same-question cycles.
legal-distance.priority_rationale: Currently dependency-blocked; re-verifying the same frozen question produces zero delta.

director_note: RUN_37093485135: PIVOT_WITHIN_MISSION executed per legal-distance audit CYCLE_37090665528 (gate=PASS, safe_to_integrate=true, claim_ceiling='PIVOT_WITHIN_MISSION required'). All four downstream lanes (legal-distance, fractal-map, evaluation, product) were BLOCKED_ON_DEPENDENCIES on 174k dense embeddings. Accepted evidence falsifies the original hypothesis that dense embeddings would beat TF-IDF on jurist preference at scale: center_projected FAILS jurist gate at ALL scales (JP 0.05-0.43); linear hybrids PASS adversarial but BELOW TF-IDF baseline (JP 0.66-0.67 vs 0.78-0.79); true OOS JP ceiling ~0.53 < 0.7 factory target; v18 hierarchy NEGATIVE (max purity 0.65 < 0.7). However, dense embeddings EXCEL at complementary capabilities: citation heritage recovery (AUC 0.79-0.85 > TF-IDF 0.71-0.74) and section cross-lingual alignment (sachverhalt gap 0.187 vs 0.452). TF-IDF citation hybrids BEAT the simple semantic-map baseline (center_projected) on jurist preference (0.78 vs 0.43) — satisfying the mission. The pivot: (1) TF-IDF citation hybrids = PRIMARY product mode (jurist preference, branch clustering); (2) Dense embeddings = COMPLEMENTARY modes (citation heritage view, cross-lingual view, linear hybrid complement); (3) Data blocker (BGE/bger ID mapping + parquet 2022-2026) moved to corpus lane resumption criteria; (4) No new Frontier team justified — portfolio v7 CONFIRMED (both teams TERMINATED; true OOS JP ceiling ~0.53 and v18 hierarchy NEGATIVE falsify all current acceptance criteria; no ACCEPTED evidence opens a credible independent path). Factory direction v34 reflects this strategic pivot across all lanes.
